capability_bindings.notes: On-box Python execution via lager python service

methods.name: input
methods.desc: Read the current state of the GPIO pin.

methods.name: output
methods.desc: Set the output state of the GPIO pin.

methods.name: wait_for_level
methods.sig: wait_for_level(level: 'int', timeout: 'float | None' = None, poll_interval: 'float' = 0.01, **kwargs) -> float
methods.desc: Block until the pin reaches the target level.

gotchas: GPIO nets are LabJack/FT232H pins — they are box-side, not DUT-side. They drive signals INTO the DUT or read signals FROM the DUT.
wait_for_level raises on timeout — wrap in try/except if you want to handle it gracefully.
GPIO.example_snippet:
from lager import Net, NetType

btn = Net.get("button1", type=NetType.GPIO)
led = Net.get("led1", type=NetType.GPIO)

# Simulate button press
btn.output(1)
import time; time.sleep(0.1)

# Check DUT reacted
assert led.input() == 1, "LED did not turn on after button press"

btn.output(0)

methods.name: clear_ocp
methods.desc: Clear an over-current protection (OCP) trip on this net.

methods.name: clear_ovp
methods.desc: Clear an over-voltage protection (OVP) trip on this net.

methods.name: current
methods.sig: current(value: 'float | None' = None, ocp: 'float | None' = None, ovp: 'float | None' = None) -> None
methods.desc: Set or read the net's current. If `value` is provided, set the output current; otherwise read and print the present current.

methods.name: disable
methods.desc: Disable (turn off) the supply output for this net.

methods.name: enable
methods.desc: Enable (turn on) the supply output for this net.

methods.name: get_full_state
methods.desc: Get full state including measurements, setpoints, and limits. This is optional and can be overridden by specific drivers.

methods.name: get_monitor_state
methods.desc: Gather the supply TUI's full monitor state in ONE call.

methods.name: ocp
methods.desc: Set or read over-current protection limit. If `value` is provided, set the OCP limit; otherwise read and print the current OCP limit.

methods.name: ovp
methods.desc: Set or read over-voltage protection limit. If `value` is provided, set the OVP limit; otherwise read and print the current OVP limit.

methods.name: set_mode
methods.desc: Set the instrument mode to DC power supply (if applicable).

methods.name: state
methods.desc: Print a comprehensive power state for this net (voltage, current, power, OCP/OVP status).

methods.name: voltage
methods.sig: voltage(value: 'float | None' = None, ocp: 'float | None' = None, ovp: 'float | None' = None) -> None
methods.desc: Set or read the net's voltage. If `value` is provided, set the output voltage; otherwise read and print the present voltage.

gotchas: Always call set_voltage() BEFORE enable() — enabling with no voltage set may use the last-programmed value.
Wrap tests in try/finally and call disable() in the finally block to avoid leaving supplies on.
Readback values may differ slightly from setpoints due to instrument resolution.
PowerSupply.example_snippet:
from lager import Net, NetType

psu = Net.get("supply1", type=NetType.PowerSupply)
try:
    psu.set_voltage(3.3)
    psu.set_current(1.0)
    psu.enable()
    import time; time.sleep(0.5)
    v = psu.voltage()
    print(f"Measured voltage: {v:.3f} V")
    assert abs(v - 3.3) < 0.2, f"Voltage out of range: {v}"
finally:
    psu.disable()

methods.name: connect
methods.desc: Connect to the UART serial port with pyserial.

methods.name: get_baudrate
methods.desc: Get the configured baudrate for this net.

methods.name: get_config
methods.desc: Get the raw net configuration dict.

methods.name: get_path
methods.desc: Get the device path for this UART net.

gotchas: connect() returns a standard pyserial Serial object — use ser.write(), ser.read(), ser.readline() etc.
Always close the serial connection when done (use try/finally or with-statement pattern).
For UART expect-style patterns: read in a loop, check for pattern match, respect timeouts.
UART.example_snippet:
from lager import Net, NetType

uart = Net.get("uart1", type=NetType.UART)
ser = uart.connect(baudrate=115200, timeout=2)
try:
    ser.reset_input_buffer()
    ser.write(b"version\r\n")
    import time; time.sleep(0.5)
    response = ser.read(ser.in_waiting).decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    print(f"DUT response: {response}")
    assert "v1." in response, f"Unexpected version: {response}"
finally:
    ser.close()
